event.summary: Removing local tmux validation is an explicit product change
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 17a3fe858c5511a24b7403af15dd41c93bf69fd7

## TLDR
The Mac app and local Linux setup stop checking for a supported tmux. This is intended because their sessions already use terminal hosts.

## Details
The assigned patch deletes TmuxSupport, probe_tmux, PATH discovery, override resolution and their tests after parse_version_component (old tmux.rs:191-665 and 757-1255). A missing local preflight is not itself a regression: SPEC_impl.md:2866-2872 explicitly says, "The supervisor runs no tmux, and neither `farhelm supervisor run` nor `farhelm helm setup` takes a `--tmux`." It further says, "The Mac app bundles none and needs none, and hands its managed supervisor no tmux." SPEC.md:3012-3014 likewise says neither the Mac app nor Linux setup needs tmux while remote Linux provisioning retains its check. Suggested bucket: other (intentional behavior, no established defect). Confidence: confirmed as specification acceptance; remaining caller consistency checks continue. proposed_drop: exact specification acceptance quoted above. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not searched. Could-be-highest: false for this candidate, which concerns removal of an unnecessary dependency check rather than an established route to security or loss of work. Caveat: this does not validate all replacement lifecycles or provisioning paths; those remain under review. Source analysis only, no execution.

Synthesis checks: traced retained host-only responsibilities at this same revision. Prompt delivery in service/core.rs:11873-11970 obtains the entry under its lifecycle claim, probes its host, requires caught-up state and bracketed-paste mode, then sends through the selected host; :2192-2232 waits for written paste before submit and bounds delivery. Initial prompts are appended to the resolved argv after placeholder/hook expansion (:14387-14398), not sent through the removed tmux probe. launch_artifacts.rs:59-76 obtains the final screen only from this entry terminal with Owned/dead evidence; it has no removed tmux lookup dependency. host_tabs.rs:1402-1432 checks the discovered tag against recorded session/tab IDs, keeping a foreign tag as an unavailable placeholder; :914-927 cross-checks the current tab runtime and excludes the agent terminal; :1012-1035 retains an unconfirmed host end as a failed tab rather than forgetting it. Provenance boundary: SPEC.md:2998-3014 and SPEC_impl.md:2784-2834 already declare old private-server retirement, screen loss, and the accepted duplicate-after-failed-termination residual; the caller also identified these as neighbouring groups known consequences. They are not discoveries in this assigned deletion. That acceptance has not been used to dismiss misleading update guidance, omitted warnings, wrong-target signals or unconfirmed Delete: this module removes only version/discovery policy helpers, and its assigned patch supplies no concrete distinct route to those effects. Original c1 wording and impact remain above. proposed_drop remains a proposal pending independent review, not an accepted drop. Could-be-highest remains false for c1 local preflight removal; no security/loss-of-work route has been established for that removal. event.summary: Deleting the three-way verdict does not remove remote Linux version enforcement
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 17a3fe858c5511a24b7403af15dd41c93bf69fd7

## TLDR
Remote Linux setup still rejects an old or unreadable host tmux and requests Farhelm's private build; deleting the local probe's classification API does not weaken that check.

## Details
Considered whether removing TmuxSupport/classify_tmux_version and their test also removed the version floor's last enforcement. Source refutes this: tmux.rs:76-80 retains the 3.7c TMUX_FLOOR; :119-184 retains exact whole-line parsing and canonical numeric/patch validation; provisioning/backend.rs:3679-3681 compares the retained parser's version directly against TMUX_FLOOR. Its caller :3915-3928 additionally requires an absolute representable tmux path and sets needs_tmux to the negated verdict. The deleted classifier's three outcomes differ from this boolean only in the above-pin warning local preflight used; the required below-floor rejection remains. Parser/order tests remain at tmux.rs:200-281 and release-pin agreement at :300-320. SPEC_impl.md, Terminal substrate: private tmux server (:2848-2864), requires the floor and accepts above-floor canonical stable releases, and specifically says, "Anything the parser cannot read exactly — `next-3.8`, release candidates, distro-decorated strings — is refused rather than guessed about: a version Farhelm cannot name is one nobody audited it against." Suggested bucket: other (source-refuted candidate). Confidence: confirmed by source; tests read, not run. proposed_drop: source refutation above; no removed enforcement found. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not searched. Could-be-highest: false: no established security or loss-of-work route from removal of this redundant verdict API. Caveat: this check concerns the deleted API's remaining production caller, not an audit of remote provisioning as a whole.

Synthesis: examined test sensitivity independently of correct production. The removed classification test exercised BelowFloor/AtFloor/AbovePin on a function and warning distinction that are deleted. Surviving responsibilities still have executable assertions: tmux.rs:203-209 distinguishes bare releases, patch letters, numeric minor order and floor identity; :225-279 distinguishes exact version lines from malformed/decorated ones; :305-318 enforces exactly one source pin and equality to the floor. provisioning.rs:6863-6875 calls the actual surviving tmux_meets_floor and asserts at-floor acceptance, above-floor acceptance, old-version rejection, and missing/unreadable-version rejection. :7909-7914, :7926-7947 and :7950-7956 assert the actual reach parser's private-payload decision for absent, old, acceptable and relative-path host tmux. These assertions would fail for replacing the surviving verdict with always-accept, always-reject, strict-greater-than, or equality-only. There is no direct remote-policy assertion for 3.7b/3.7d in the inspected test, but the former local classification test did not invoke that remote function either; its deletion does not establish a new end-to-end sensitivity gap. This is source analysis of assertions, not mutation testing or test execution. The deleted probe containment/PATH/override tests concern removed code; no surviving production caller of their deleted API was found.

Suggested bucket: other (source-refuted candidate). Confidence: confirmed by source; tests read, not run. proposed_drop: source refutation and separate surviving-test sensitivity checks above; pending independent decision, not accepted. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not searched. Could-be-highest: false: no established security or loss-of-work route from removal of this redundant verdict API. Caveat: this check concerns the deleted API's remaining production caller and test responsibilities, not an audit of remote provisioning as a whole.
